chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, in the questions of Ismail ibn Isa, from Al-Akhir, regarding an owned slave who disobeys his master,
'Is it permissible to whip him or not?' So he said: 'It is not permissible for you to whip him; if he is compatible with you, keep him, or else release him.'

key_terms.إِنْ وَافَقَكَ: if he is compatible with you

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on whipping a disobedient slave?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic principle that a master's right to discipline a slave is not absolute but contingent upon the nature of the disobedience. It establishes a binary choice: if the act is minor or compatible with the master's authority, the master may retain and correct the slave; if it is significant or unjust, the master must release him, emphasizing justice over arbitrary power. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the moral and legal status of slaves as individuals with rights, rather than mere property.
